UPDATED AGAIN 2026-07-26: THIS FILE IS NO LONGER ANYTHING'S SOURCE OF TRUTH. It is a record of what was done and why. The live answer to "which names are published" is GET /api/registry/published, which enumerates MiniAppRegistry.totalApps()/page() on 0G and filters to the configured parent; the Registry page reads that route on every mount. This list existed as a de facto source of truth and drifted twice — it omitted the flagship once, and it disagreed with the contract by two entries when the enumeration route was built. A hand-maintained list of onchain facts drifts; that is the whole reason the route exists.

manifestAvailability.note: RESOLVED 2026-07-26. Three names had a contenthash whose bytes were gone: they were published while IPFS_MODE=local, whose content store (web/.atlas/, gitignored) was the only provider, so ipfs.io returned 504 permanently — a CID is the hash of its bytes, so regenerating the manifest yields a different CID that no longer matches the chain. Unrecoverable by pinning, which is why they were re-published instead. IMPORTANT, and the reason this is not called a restoration: the original manifests are gone for good. scripts/publish-under-parent.ts regenerates a plan from an intent through the real planner, so what those three names now carry is a FRESH plan for the same intent, not the document they used to point at. IPFS_MODE is now pinata so the loss cannot recur. Note also that a freshly pinned CID takes minutes to become retrievable through ipfs.io even though Pinata serves it immediately — a 504 on a new publish is propagation, not loss, and the two look identical for the first few minutes.
manifestAvailability.resolvesNote: Every name issued under this parent was read back through GET /api/resolve/<label> on 2026-07-26: addr set, manifest fetched, and — for the seven registered under the current parent — mutuallyVerified true. This list is a snapshot and is not what anything reads: the live answer is GET /api/registry/published, which enumerates MiniAppRegistry.

orphanedTokens.note: Agentic ID tokens that are still minted and still owned, but which no live ENS name asserts any more. Tokens 5, 6 and 7 were bound to aave-health-guard, wallet-bound-guard and attested-market-guard under the OLD parent (*.graphminis.eth). When those three names were re-published on 2026-07-26 they had to take new tokens, because MiniAppRegistry.register reverts TokenAlreadyBound and AgenticId._bindEnsName reverts EnsNameAlreadyBound — a binding you can silently move is not a binding. So the old tokens are not revoked and not reused; they simply no longer correspond to anything resolvable. Their MiniAppRegistry entries are three of the six that GET /api/registry/published reports as `retired`.

registryGap.note: Names whose ENS records and Agentic ID are live but which MiniAppRegistry does not assert under this parent, so mutuallyVerified reads false and the Published names strip does not show them. Checked 2026-07-26 by reading get(nameKey) off 0G Galileo and by GET /api/resolve/<label>. aave-guard-fork: registerFork reverted ParentUnknown and the revert was swallowed — cause and fix in its note above; left as-is because it is the evidence. durable-market-guard: never re-published, so its token still names the old parent; its manifest fetches, which is why it was outside the re-publish that covered the three names whose bytes were lost.
